healthBenefits.title: Lean Protein Source
healthBenefits.text: Octopus is low in fat and rich in high-quality protein, supporting muscle repair and growth.

healthBenefits.title: Energizing Carbohydrates
healthBenefits.text: Potatoes provide complex carbohydrates and potassium, helping maintain energy levels and healthy blood pressure.

healthBenefits.title: Fiber-Rich Vegetables
healthBenefits.text: Green beans add dietary fiber and vitamins A and C, supporting digestion and immune function.

healthBenefits.title: Vitamin C Boost
healthBenefits.text: Lemon juice enhances iron absorption and provides a strong dose of immune-supporting vitamin C.

healthBenefits.title: Heart-Healthy Fats
healthBenefits.text: Extra virgin olive oil contributes monounsaturated fats and antioxidants that support cardiovascular health.

healthBenefits.title: Digestive Aid
healthBenefits.text: Mint and garlic offer digestive benefits and natural antimicrobial properties.

_ingredientsText:
1 octopus (about 700 g)
• 3 potatoes, diced into cubes
• 300 g of green beans, cleaned
• juice of 1 lemon
• 1 clove of garlic, chopped or crushed
• 10 mint leaves, chopped
• 3 tablespoons extra virgin olive oil
• salt
_preparationText:
Wash the octopus in cold water, then put it in a pot of cold water. Let it cook for 30 minutes, adding salt after it is finished cooking.
2. Drain the octopus and let it cool on a plate. Then cut it into small pieces.
3. Separately, wash the green beans and boil them in salted water for about 8 minutes.
4. Remove the green beans from the cooking water with a strainer spoon, then, in the same cooking water, add the diced potatoes and cook for 10 minutes.
5. Drain and let cool.
6. In a large bowl, put the rest of the
ingredients together: pieces of octopus, vegetables, lemon juice, garlic (either crushed or diced), grated lemon peel, mint leaves and olive oil.
